Join us in this role where you’ll originate and build new ventures from the ground up, turning bold ideas into scalable businesses. You’ll shape opportunities, validate them with the market, and drive early commercialisation, working across functions and leveraging the strength of a global organisation.

**Welcome to Ventures & Open Innovation

**You’ll be part of a team focused on identifying and scaling transformational opportunities, where you together with your colleagues will explore new markets, business models, and technologies. You’ll collaborate closely across engineering, commercial, and business development functions to bring new ideas to life. As a team, we support each other, challenge ideas constructively, and work with curiosity and ownership to turn ambition into impact.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• originating new business opportunities by identifying white spaces and shaping opportunity areas

• leading end-to-end venture building from ideation through validation to early commercialisation

• designing and testing business models through structured experimentation and rapid learning

• collaborating with internal stakeholders to unlock capabilities and move opportunities forward

• translating technical assets and capabilities into new commercial propositions

• contributing to innovation strategy and portfolio prioritisation.

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• have hands-on experience building new businesses or ventures from concept to launch

• bring a strong commercial mindset, focusing on customers, value creation, and revenue models

• are comfortable working across ambiguity and can create structure and direction independently

• collaborate effectively with both technical and commercial stakeholders, or equivalent experience

• demonstrate curiosity and quickly build understanding in new industries or domains

• communicate clearly and persuasively, building alignment around new ideas.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country.

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is kr62,160.00- kr93,240.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11% contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3% holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and wellbeing programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

**Pre-employment background check:

**Certain positions may require a background check as part of the hiring process. If applicable, you will be informed during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

Do you enjoy turning business requirements and market insights into sourcing opportunities that create value for the organization? Join Ambu’s Global Indirect Procurement & Capex team and play an important role in supporting procurement across an international, fast-growing organization.

As Associate Category Manager, you will support sourcing and category management activities across indirect Procurement. Working closely with experienced Global Category Managers, you will lead or contribute to sourcing projects, supplier management activities, market analyses and stakeholder engagement while developing your sourcing & category management capabilities. You will gradually take ownership of defined sourcing activities and projects while building experience across the source-to-contract process.

You will join an ambitious global procurement organization where your work will have visible business impact. The role offers broad exposure to international stakeholders, varied indirect categories and end-to-end sourcing activities, providing a unique opportunity to build experience across a global procurement environment.

The position is based at Ambu’s headquarters in Ballerup and reports to the Director of Global Indirect Procurement & Capex.

**Key Responsibilities

**Your main responsibilities will include:

• Support the translation of business requirements and market insights into sourcing strategies and recommendations.

• Contribute to or lead RFI, RFQ and RFP processes, including supplier identification, market analysis, preparation of sourcing documentation, proposal evaluation and stakeholder coordination.

• Independently manage defined sourcing activities and less complex sourcing events using established procurement processes and tools.

• Support supplier negotiations, contract preparation and contract handover activities.

• Analyze spend, suppliers, markets and cost drivers to identify savings opportunities, value creation initiatives and risk considerations.

• Prepare sourcing analyses, recommendations and business case inputs for stakeholder decision-making.

• Build productive relationships with stakeholders, suppliers and cross-functional partners, collaborating closely with Global Category Managers and function including Legal, Quality Assurance, Finance and IT.

• Support continuous improvement initiatives, digital procurement activities and the adoption of new procurement tools and processes.

**Suggested candidate profile

****Skills

**Skills and experiences can be earned in many different ways, and we understand that the best fit for the role cannot be prescribed on paper. You are however likely to succeed in this position if you:

• Hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree within Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Economics, Finance or a related field.

• Bring 2-3 years of experience within procurement, sourcing, category management or a related procurement function.

• Have experience supporting sourcing initiatives, supplier management activities or procurement projects.

• Understand source-to-contract processes and are comfortable working with stakeholders across different functions.

• Possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn data and market insights into recommendations.

• Are a structured and proactive team player with strong communication and project coordination skills, including solid Excel and Microsoft Office capabilities.

• Communicate fluently in English and are motivated to learn and grow within a global procurement organization. Experience with sourcing platforms (e.g. Keelvar, Coupa, Ariba, GEP or similar) as well as an interest in digital procurement, AI or process automation is considered an advantage.

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**Ambu is a company that expands rapidly and has ambitious growth targets. We meet these targets through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international head office with an informal working environment.

We offer great opportunities for personal development. Furthermore, we offer a wide range of professional, social and financial employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

jobs.occupation: Specialist - Energy, Indoor Climate and Daylight
jobs.description:
**Do you want to contribute to create healthy, energy-efficient, and sustainable buildings? Do you have experience in indoor climate design and energy optimization for complex building projects? Perhaps you have just a few years of experience or perhaps you are a senior specialist - the important thing is that you are motivated to apply your expertise and curiosity to develop solutions that enable a better tomorrow.

**

**Turn challenges into sustainable solutions

**

At COWI, we help our clients create attractive, comfortable, and sustainable buildings through energy optimization, indoor climate design, and daylight analysis. To grow our team, we are looking for a Specialist in Energy, Indoor Climate and Daylight to join our growing group of approximately 30 colleagues. Together, we work on exciting and complex projects across the building, industrial, pharmaceutical, and transformation sectors.

In this position, you will become part of an established, highly collaborative professional environment across COWI and Arkitema. We deliver energy calculations, indoor climate simulations, daylight analyses, and sustainability advisory services.

You will work closely with experts across multiple disciplines on both new-build projects and the transformation of existing buildings. Our interdisciplinary collaboration is one of our greatest advantages, enabling us to continuously raise the bar for sustainability across the industry

**Your key activities will be:

**

• Contribute to the design and optimization of energy-efficient, healthy, and sustainable buildings for both new construction and renovation projects.

• Carry out energy, indoor climate, and daylight simulations and analyses using tools such as IES VE, Rhino/Grasshopper, and similar software.

• Collaborate closely with architects, engineers, sustainability specialists, and clients to develop integrated design solutions.

• Support project managers and discipline leads in delivering high-quality technical solutions.

• Participate in technical development and knowledge sharing within the team.

• Contribute to innovation and the continuous improvement of our methods, tools, and services.

• Depending on your experience, take responsibility for smaller assignments or specific technical work packages within larger projects.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future

**

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. You should also be open to new perspectives and continuously seek opportunities to learn, innovate, and improve.

**On top of that, you will:

**

• Have at least three years of experience in indoor climate simulations, building performance analysis, and/or energy optimization within construction, building operations, or industry.

• Have experience working on projects in Denmark and be familiar with Danish building regulations.

• Be comfortable managing your own tasks while making a contribution to multidisciplinary project teams.

• Have professional proficiency in at least one Scandinavian language, both written and spoken.

• Take a collaborative and professional approach to working with colleagues, clients, and business partners.

• Demonstrate high integrity and a willingness to share knowledge and support the professional development of others.

**A place to work and so much more

**

At COWI, we work together with our customers to build a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and most importantly our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. That is why we say no to fossil-based projects and aspire to have most of our revenue come from activities that move our customers towards sustainability.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in Scandinavia, the UK, North America and India, we are currently 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve, and what life is like at COWI.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key.

**

We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

jobs.occupation: Finance Partner for Financial Planning & Analytics department at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
If you're energised by turning data into valuable insights and thrive on teamwork in a dynamic environment, we'd love to hear from you!

**Who We Are

**We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

**About The Role

**We are looking for a Finance Partner to join our Financial Planning & Analytics DK team. As trusted partners to the organization, we deliver timely, accurate, and data-driven insights that enable informed decision-making and efficient resource allocation.

Our mission is to empower the business to focus on its core responsibilities while driving performance.

In this role, you will leverage advanced analytics, financial modelling, and digital tools to provide actionable insights and collaborate closely with business leaders to shape strategic decisions. We offer a steep learning curve, exposure to advanced analytics and digital tools, and the chance to develop into a trusted partner for the organization, as long as you are curious, proactive, and eager to learn.

Location Denmark - Virum

Experience 0 - 2 years

Department Financial Planning & Analytics

**How You Might Spend Your Days

**As a Finance Partner you’ll be:

• Analysing large datasets and transforming them into meaningful insights that support management decisions

• Driving forecasting, budgeting, and scenario planning using advanced planning tools and BI platforms

• Acting as the primary financial advisor for a VP and managers in the line of business, ensuring clarity and transparency in financial performance

• Optimizing financial processes through automation and digitalization, ensuring efficiency and accuracy

• Participating in rotational tasks across planning, reporting, and performance analysis to broaden your impact and expertise

• Collaborating on data governance and quality initiatives, ensuring reliable inputs for strategic planning.

**Who You Are

**We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• A data-savvy problem solver with great analytical skills and a passion for turning numbers into actionable insights

• Comfortable with complex datasets, able to structure and interpret data to tell a clear story

• A good communicator who can simplify technical findings and constructively challenge stakeholders at all levels

• Proactive, structured, and detail-oriented, while maintaining a strategic overview

• Agile and adaptable, thriving in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities

• A collaborative team player who values knowledge sharing and cross-functional cooperation

**What You Bring To The Role

**In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• M.Sc degree within economics or finance with excellent results

• 1-2 years of experience performing management reporting and planning budget processes.

• Experience in financial systems, BI tools, and data visualization (e.g., Power BI)

• You speak and write English

**Why choose NNE?

**NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer **here .

****Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

****Deadline of application is 18th November 2026

**Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Manager Rasmus Moltved on +45 3077 4638.

**Please note:

**

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

**Fair hiring:

**At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

**Still searching for the right opportunity?

**If this position isn’t quite what you're looking for, but you know someone who would excel in this role, please share this job post. And don’t forget to explore our other exciting opportunities — your future role at NNE might be just around the corner! Visit our Career Site

jobs.occupation: Senior Manager, Technology & Innovation - Control & Connectivity Solutions
jobs.description:
**The Impact You'll Make

**As our new Senior Manager, Technology & Innovation, you will shape the future of control systems used in off-road mobile machinery around the world. Leading a team of Architects and Innovation Engineers, you will define and drive the technology roadmap for next-generation Controllers, Displays, Remote Controls, and Joysticks, helping create the technologies that will power safer, more productive, connected, and increasingly autonomous machines.

This role combines people leadership, technology strategy, system architecture, and innovation. Working across our global Engineering and Portfolio organizations, you will turn customer needs, market trends, regulatory requirements, and emerging technologies into scalable platform solutions that enable future product development. You'll have the opportunity to influence key technology decisions, develop talented teams, and help bring new technologies from early exploration into real-world customer value.

The position is ideally based at one of our Danfoss Power Solutions locations in Northern Europe, with flexibility for other locations where local employment regulations allow.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Define and drive the technology and innovation roadmap for our Control & Connectivity Solutions portfolio, ensuring it supports future product and platform strategies.

• Lead, coach, and develop a team of Architects and Innovation Engineers, creating an environment built on collaboration, accountability, technical excellence, and continuous learning.

• Own and govern key architecture principles and technology choices for future generations of Controllers, Displays, Remote Controls, and Joysticks.

• Build and manage a technology pipeline that moves ideas from exploration and proof-of-concept through technology maturation and handover into product development.

• Translate customer, market, regulatory, and technology trends into engineering opportunities, working closely with Portfolio Management, Product Management, Engineering, and Procurement teams across the global organization.

**What We're Looking For

**

• Experience leading and developing technical teams within engineering, technology, innovation, or product development environments.

• Great experience developing embedded and connected mechatronic systems that integrate electronics, embedded software, communication technologies, and mechanical design.

• Expertise in defining technology strategies, system architectures, technology roadmaps, or product platforms for complex products and systems.

• Understanding of functional safety, machinery regulations, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance within embedded industrial, automotive, mobile machinery, or similarly regulated environments.

• Ability to collaborate, influence decisions, and build effective relationships across global, cross-functional organizations.

**What You'll Get From Us

**

• You'll lead a highly skilled technical team and influence the technologies and architectures behind future generations of machine control solutions.

• You'll work closely with senior leaders across Engineering and Portfolio Management, giving you visibility and impact on key technology and product decisions.

• You'll gain exposure to emerging technologies and help turn new ideas into scalable solutions used by customers around the world.

• We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities. You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected and valued for who they are.

• You’ll receive benefits like annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about, we think they’re pretty great.

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If you're excited by the opportunity to shape technology strategy, lead talented engineers, and help create the next generation of intelligent machine control solutions, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

**Our Commitment to Transparency

**Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our **FAQ Page.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

Are you passionate about developing people and helping leaders succeed? PEAK Wind is seeking a Lead People & Development Specialist to strengthen leadership development, lead larger people initiatives, and provide trusted guidance on complex people matters. This is a senior generalist role for someone who combines hands-on experience with the confidence to turn business needs into practical solutions.

Introducing the People & Development Team

You will become part of our People & Development team, where we work collaboratively to attract, develop, and retain talented colleagues and support the business across the employee lifecycle. We share knowledge, support one another, and bring different perspectives to finding solutions that work for both our people and our business.

You will report to Head of People & Development and work closely with our Senior Management, leaders and colleagues across the business. As an experienced individual contributor, you will take ownership of your areas of responsibility while contributing to the wider team’s priorities.

How You Will Make an Impact

As a Lead People & Development Specialist, you will combine broad generalist responsibilities with a strong focus on leadership development and project delivery. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Support the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of leadership development initiatives, translating leaders’ needs into practical workshops, tools, and follow-up activities.

• Act as a trusted sparring partner to Senior Management and  leaders on team development, performance, collaboration, and day-to-day people decisions.

• Lead larger, cross-functional People & Development projects from scoping and planning through implementation and follow-up, managing stakeholders, dependencies, and communication.

• Handle complex and sensitive employee relations cases with sound judgement, discretion, and a structured approach, involving relevant colleagues or external advisers when needed.

• Contribute across the employee lifecycle, providing pragmatic guidance and supporting consistent people practices, policies, and processes.

• Support annual people processes, including Performance & Development Dialogues and Talent Reviews, helping leaders turn discussions into meaningful development actions.

• Identify opportunities to improve how we work and share your experience with the People & Development team to strengthen our collective delivery.

What Will Make You Successful in This Role

You are an experienced People & Development generalist who enjoys both developing people and navigating the complexity of everyday people matters. You can work independently, build trust with leaders, and balance longer-term development initiatives with hands-on delivery. You will bring:

• A relevant educational background in human resources, organisational development, psychology, business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Substantial experience in a broad HR or People & Development role, with the judgement and independence to operate as a senior generalist.

• Hands-on experience supporting leadership development, including facilitating learning activities and helping leaders apply new approaches in practice.

• A track record of leading larger people projects with multiple stakeholders, from defining the need to embedding the outcome.

• Experience handling complex employee relations cases with empathy, confidentiality, and sound judgement, recognising when specialist or legal advice is needed.

• Strong relationship-building and facilitation skills, with the confidence to support and constructively challenge leaders.

• A structured, pragmatic approach and the ability to prioritise competing needs and follow through on commitments.

• Clear and effective communication skills in English, both spoken and written, and a collaborative mindset.

• Experience working with Insights profiles in individual or team development is a clear advantage; relevant accreditation is welcome but not required.

Why Join PEAK Wind

• An international, inclusive, and diverse workplace where differences are valued

• The opportunity to strengthen leadership and people practices in a business supporting the renewable energy transition

• Flexible working arrangements that support both your career and personal life

• A flat organisational structure where your ideas are welcomed and your contributions matter

• A strong focus on your learning, development, and professional growth.

• A culture that values commitment, meaningful contributions, and having fun

Our Commitment to Inclusion and Fair Hiring

We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace drives innovation, creativity, and stronger results. At PEAK Wind, we are committed to fair and transparent hiring processes, welcoming candidates from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Our hiring decisions focus on what each person brings to the role and our team, and we are committed to ensuring transparent salary structures, with pay decisions based on clear, objective, and gender‑neutral criteria. Salary information, including the relevant salary band, will be shared with candidates when they are invited to a first interview.

How to Apply

We look forward to receiving your application. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the recruitment process once the right candidate has been found. Please apply directly through our website. If you have any questions or would like to know more about the position, please contact People & Development at recruitment@peak-wind.com.

About PEAK Wind

PEAK Wind is an independent renewable energy specialist in commercial, financial, and technical operations, delivering advisory, intelligence, and asset management services to investors and developers around the world. From onshore and offshore wind generation to Power-to-X, we work across the entire energy lifecycle to optimise operations and maintenance, enhance asset performance, and provide a holistic view of renewable infrastructure portfolios.

Our values - Expertise, Passion, Unity, and Integrity - are reflected in everything we do, from how we support our clients to how we collaborate as a team. At PEAK Wind, you will be able to apply your professional skills in a dynamic environment and experience a meaningful responsibility and involvement.

jobs.occupation: QA Specialist, QA Commercial Drug Substance
jobs.description:
Are you experienced in managing CMO collaborations and building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders? Do you thrive in a broad QA role where you combine your GMP expertise with a pragmatic and hands-on approach across different quality areas?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new QA Specialist in QA Commercial Operations.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate QA specialist to join our team. You will be a part of the well-functioning QA Drug Substance/QA for QC team in the QA Commercial Operations department, with responsibility for quality oversight of starting materials, intermediates, and Drug Substances for commercial products. We have a close collaboration with our Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) and process- and QC SMEs internally at Ascendis Pharma.

Your key responsibilities will be:

As part of the role, you will work broadly across quality oversight activities and take ownership of a wide range of tasks and responsibilities, including:

• Take primary responsibility for oversight of one or more CMOs in our supply chains with respect to review and approval of documentation from these CMOs, including upscale activities, PPQ documentation, CPVs, batch documentation, deviations, changes, CAPAs, stability studies, QMRs, quality agreements etc

• Build and maintain strong relationships with key CMO stakeholders, ensuring clear communication and effective collaboration through meetings, teleconferences, and audits. Participate in CMO evaluations and product quality reviews

• Keep up to date with changes in relevant product guidelines and regulatory requirements and ensure cGMP at Ascendis and CMOs

• Drive and assume responsibility for agreed tasks and matters

• Continuously optimize our work processes and the way we execute quality oversight

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree - preferably a master's degree in pharmacy or equivalent - and 5-10 years of experience within chemical and/or biological GMP production

Furthermore, you have:

• Solid QA experience, preferably including QA for QC, and experience working with CMOs

• Strong analytical skills, a collaborative mindset, and a can-do attitude

• Cultural understanding

• Experience with audits/inspections

• A critical and pragmatic mindset and yet with attention to the necessary details

• Clear and persistent communication skills, particular regarding expectations and requirements to quality

• Cooperative and striving for smooth cooperation with many stakeholders

• Ambitious and able to see the benefits in going the extra mile

The position as QA specialist requires experience with and knowledge of US and EU GMP regulations and requirements. Furthermore, you should be proficient in English at a professional level, both written and spoken, and you master MS Office.

At Ascendis Pharma, you will be part of a stimulating, informal, and innovative working environment, where you will interact with very skilled colleagues and partners to deliver on Ascendis' ambitious corporate goals. You will be part of an expanding QA-organization overseeing development, clinical, and commercial activities.

Travel: 5-20 days/year.

Place of work: Tuborg Boulevard 12, Hellerup

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the job or the company, please contact QA Senior Director, Jan Jakobsgaard, M +45 25 66 29 42 leave a message if call is not answered. All applications must be submitted in English and are treated confidentially.

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

A note to recruiters:

We do not allow external search party solicitation. Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team (specifically from: Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director) is not allowed. **Your impact begins here

**As Sr Manager, LIMS and Ecosystems, you will lead the team responsible for LIMS (Laboratory IT Management Systems) and Ecosystems, giving people clear direction and turning departmental plans into priorities they can act on today. You will build a team that is well staffed, growing and accountable, and work with IT and business partners to secure reliable, compliant delivery. Your impact will be felt in a team that performs consistently and in the colleagues who rely on its work.

**What You’ll Bring

**You are a people leader who sets direction, follows through and keeps teams moving, in a complex and regulated environment.

• A Master’s degree or equivalent relevant education. Substantial relevant experience may compensate for formal education requirements.

• Relevant people-leadership experience, including goal setting, delegation, performance management, development and employee relations.

• Experience leading professional employees and coordinating assignments of medium to high complexity.

• Experience translating departmental plans into operational goals, priorities and follow-up.

• Experience with workforce and capacity planning, recruitment and FTE-related budget management.

• Experience working with IT and business stakeholders in a complex, regulated organisation.

• The ability to communicate clearly, make timely decisions, work independently and handle conflicts and difficult conversations constructively.

• An inclusive mindset that respects different perspectives and reflects The Novo Way.

• Novo leadership training, or willingness to complete the required leadership training.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**Knowledge of laboratory systems, enterprise IT or adjacent regulated-business domains.

**What You’ll Do

**You will be the first-line leader for the LIMS and Ecosystems area, accountable for how the team performs, develops and delivers.

• Set clear expectations and goals for the team and each employee, and hold regular one-to-ones, team meetings and performance dialogues.

• Turn LAPS priorities into team plans, milestones and follow-up routines, balancing planned work, operational support and emerging issues based on business impact, risk and capacity.

• Act as hiring manager, plan the team’s future skills and capacity, and ensure structured onboarding, development plans, succession and career conversations.

• Own the team’s FTE-related budget and the system budgets for the area, and recommend adjustments when demand and capacity are not balanced.

• Make sure procedures, quality requirements and information security expectations are understood and followed, and that risks and compliance concerns are raised and acted on early.

• Simplify team routines, roles and interfaces, and lead agreed changes until they are embedded.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Enterprise IT & Quality, where colleagues work across the Novo value chain, stay close to stakeholders and help deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working. This is the department of Laboratory and PAT solutions, where colleagues deliver IT solutions and drive digitalization for laboratories and quality control across Novo globally.

You will lead a team of professional employees in LIMS and Ecosystems and take part in the LAPS Leadership Team, aligning priorities, capacity and dependencies with your peer leaders. Day to day, you will work with Product Management, system and solution roles, business representatives and colleagues in EIT (Enterprise IT) and Line of Business to set expectations, share delivery status and resolve issues. HR and finance partners will support you on recruitment, performance, reward, workforce planning and budget.

You will be the first escalation point for team matters, and you will make sure decisions, risks and escalations reach the right level quickly and clearly.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will be trusted to work independently within agreed objectives and to make decisions for your team. Clear performance expectations, honest feedback and a culture that recognises results will help you perform at your best, and you will have the chance to grow your own leadership through Novo’s leadership training.

RESOLVA is assisting INVISIO with the recruitment of a Corporate Legal Counsel.

ROLE DESCRIPTION

INVISIO is looking for a commercially minded and pragmatic Corporate Legal Counsel to support its global business. This is a broad legal generalist role with a strong commercial focus, where you will work closely with the business and provide legal support across a wide range of matters, with particular emphasis on international contracts, tenders, customer projects and other commercial legal matters.

As Corporate Legal Counsel, you will become part of a small legal team together with Signe Karstoft, Legal Director, to whom you will report. The role is based at INVISIO’s headquarters in Hvidovre, and the legal function is organisationally anchored within INVISIO’s Sales & Program function, which consists of approximately 50 employees globally, including around 25-30 in Denmark. You will primarily support the global sales organisation and work closely with colleagues across the business. Much of your work will involve large and complex customer contracts, tenders and projects.

You will provide legal support across INVISIO’s international business, including in relation to US contracts, such as contracts within the defence sector, and support sales teams across Europe and other markets. You will also support INVISIO in connection with major public tenders, including tenders involving ministries and defence organisations, providing legal support on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

As a technology company, intellectual property is an important part of INVISIO’s business. While dedicated specialists handle areas such as patents, you may also advise on IP-related matters as part of the broader commercial legal support. Experience with IP or from a technology or other IP-intensive business would therefore be an advantage.

In addition to the day-to-day legal support, you will contribute to developing and improving the way Legal supports the business. This includes driving legal improvement initiatives, maintaining and developing contract templates and legal guidelines, and conducting workshops and awareness activities for the business.

The role is highly international and outward-facing, with significant interaction with customers and stakeholders at all levels. You will have opportunities to join customer visits and negotiate contracts abroad, as well as participate in trade fairs in Denmark, Europe and the US.

The role is expected to involve approximately 25 travel days per year.

As INVISIO continues to grow rapidly, you will work in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, and no two days are the same.

AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

INVISIO is looking for an independent and commercially minded lawyer who takes ownership and enjoys working closely with customers and colleagues across the organisation. Your key responsibilities will include:

Commercial contracts and negotiations:

• 
Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of commercial contracts, including large international sales contracts, non-disclosure agreements, letters of intent, consulting agreements, tender-related contracts and distribution agreements.

• 
Take an active role in customer dialogue and contract negotiations and provide commercially focused legal advice, working closely with relevant stakeholders to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives.

• 
Provide pragmatic legal advice on contractual and other commercial matters arising in the day-to-day business.

Tenders and customer projects:

• 
Provide legal support in connection with major public tenders, including reviewing tender documentation and advising on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

• 
Advise on legal and contractual aspects of tender structures, including which INVISIO entity should participate and any related intercompany arrangements.

• 
Support and, where relevant, take a coordinating role in customer projects and other commercial initiatives, including advising on contractual set-ups, priorities and how existing solutions can be applied in different markets etc.

IP and export control:

• Ad hoc Advise on IP and export control matters, including IP considerations in commercial agreements and questions relating to export restrictions and requirements in connection with international sales and customer projects.

Legal development and business support:

• 
Develop, maintain and improve contract templates, legal guidelines and other tools.

• 
Drive legal improvement initiatives and conduct workshops and legal awareness activities for the business, for example in relation to NDA’s.

• 
Provide ad hoc legal advice and support across INVISIO as required.

REPORTING AND TITLE

Reporting to: Signe Karstoft, Legal Director.

Title: Corporate Legal Counsel.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

Education: You hold a master’s degree in law (cand.jur. or cand.merc.jur).

Work experience: You have approximately 3-6 years of relevant legal experience from an in-house role, for example in a technology or software company or another larger international industrial company.

Legal areas of specialisation: You have strong experience in drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements and are comfortable handling contractual matters independently. You also have experience supporting tender processes and advising on the legal and contractual matters that arise in this context.

In addition, you have a broad legal profile and are able to navigate a varied range of legal matters. Experience with IP-related matters, particularly from a technology or other IP-intensive business, would be an advantage. Knowledge of export control would also be beneficial.

Commercial: You have a strong commercial mindset and understand how legal advice fits into the broader business context.

You have experience working directly with customers and are comfortable collaborating with colleagues at all levels of the organisation. You are able to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives and provide pragmatic, solution-oriented advice.

Language skills: You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and verbal.

PERSONAL CAPABILITIES

Independent & proactive: You work independently, take ownership of your responsibilities and proactively drive matters forward.

Outgoing & interpersonal: You are outgoing and enjoy interacting with people with different backgrounds and at all levels, both internally and externally. You have strong interpersonal skills and are comfortable engaging with customers, colleagues and senior management.

Analytical & pragmatic: You have strong analytical skills and are able to understand complex legal and commercial matters while maintaining a pragmatic and solution-oriented approach.

Structured & able to prioritise: You work in a structured manner, maintain a good overview of your responsibilities and are able to prioritise effectively in a fast-paced environment where new and urgent matters frequently arise. You remain calm and focused when priorities change or deadlines are tight.

Stakeholder management & collaboration: You build strong relationships and collaborate effectively across functions and organisational levels. You are a team-oriented colleague who contributes to a strong sense of teamwork across the organisation and is able to influence stakeholders in a constructive manner.

Positive & constructive: You have a professional approach to your work and interact with others with maturity and integrity. You bring positive energy, are resilient when challenges arise and remain constructive in a busy environment.

INVISIO’S VALUE PROPOSITION TO YOU

INVISIO is a rapidly growing company with ambitious growth targets. The company achieves these ambitions through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts will be important to INVISIO’s continued success, and by joining the company, you will become part of an international headquarter with an informal working environment.

INVISIO offers a wide range of professional and social employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

ABOUT INVISIO

INVISIO is a global leader in communications technology for professionals working in mission-critical environments. Established in Denmark in 1999, the company develops and markets advanced, integrated communication systems for defence and public safety professionals, helping users communicate clearly and safely in demanding environments.

INVISIO’s modular and scalable portfolio includes headsets, control units, intercom systems, hubs and software designed to work together across dismounted, vehicle-based and command operations. The solutions are marketed under the INVISIO and Racal Acoustics brands.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, INVISIO has an international presence across Europe, North America and Asia. The company has approximately 330 employees globally, including around 215 in Denmark, and is growing rapidly. INVISIO is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (Large Cap).

INVISIO is characterised by a strong focus on innovation, close customer collaboration and an international working environment. Its core values are Passion, Innovation, Teamwork and Customer First.

You can learn more about INVISIO here: www.invisio.com.

APPLICATION AND CONTACT

If you believe this position is a good fit for you, we look forward to receiving your application. Please attach your CV and any relevant documentation. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please don’t hesitate to contact Camilla Krogh at (+45 51261264) or Mikkel Falkenberg at (+45 29993065) from the team at RESOLVA.

jobs.occupation: Outsourcing Project Director - Drug Substance Outsourcing
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Project Director, you will lead the most complex sourcing projects in Drug Substance, from category strategy through to signed contracts with CMOs, where commitments can exceed DKK 1 billion. You will shape strategies for areas of growing importance to Novo, such as synthetic peptides, and negotiate partnerships that are strong commercially and sustainable over time. Your work helps keep the supply of treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases reliable.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior sourcing and project leader who combines a strategic mindset with an eye for contractual detail.

**You Have

**

• A university master’s degree in pharmacy, biology, engineering, supply chain management, law or business.

• Around 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical experience, in manufacturing, manufacturing development and/or CMO environments. The role may suit candidates with around 20 years of experience.

• A strong background in strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and external partner management.

• Solid experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, as project and/or line manager.

• In-depth knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing, CMOs, quality and regulatory requirements.

• Excellent negotiation and contracting skills, and the ability to engage with senior management and CMO executives, up to CEO level.

• The ability to lead and influence without formal authority, with resilience, autonomy, a sense of urgency and strong execution skills.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Supplementary training in areas such as cGMP, project execution or personal development.

• An existing network within Novo, CMOs and pharmaceutical engineering companies.

• Experience in Drug Product sourcing.

What you’ll do

You will own sourcing projects from the first idea to final implementation, and you will keep strategy, contract and delivery pointing in the same direction.

**In Practice, You Will

**

• Develop category strategies for areas of strategic importance, such as synthetic peptides, by pairing market insight, including global players and trends, with Novo’s strategic outlook.

• Lead critical CMO negotiations independently until signature, securing outcomes within mandate that balance value, cost, flexibility, speed and risk.

• Drive projects end-to-end: set up governance and Steering Committees, build business cases and plans, define deliverables and manage risk.

• Bring together specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance and Legal, and raise bottlenecks early so work keeps moving.

• Keep SVP and EVP-level stakeholders informed and aligned on progress, and give input to business plans and budgets.

• Raise the standard for how Drug Substance Outsourcing works by sharing your approach with category managers and developing sourcing standards.

Who you’ll work with

You will be a senior individual contributor in GSOD Drug Substance Outsourcing, reporting to the Senior Director of the department. The role has no direct reports, but you will lead through influence: category groups and project teams with specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Finance and Legal, as well as colleagues in Global Contract Manufacturing DS, Supply Chain Design, GMS Management and country affiliates.

Externally, you will work with CMOs across the US, Europe and Asia, so you should expect to spend significant time abroad. You will balance partnership and long-term collaboration with the best possible commercial terms for Novo, and you will be at ease handling cross-cultural discussions when tension runs high.

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them. Your primary focus will be Drug Substance, with potential involvement in Drug Product and Devices.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take decisions independently and to give strategic guidance to senior leaders on the project portfolio. You will build new skills through cross-functional and cross-border work, and you will be recognised for results through clear performance expectations.

You will also have room to challenge convention: to find faster, better ways to run projects and to shape new processes and standards for CMO partnerships.

The pay range for this role is 940,800 – 1,448,700 DKK per year. The final offer reflects your experience and qualifications.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Novo’s most strategic CMO partnerships from strategy to signature, apply for the Project Director role by 19st November 2026 . We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Uffe Holme ufho@novonordisk.com
